AK.key_factor: The ballot's second 'Sullivan' plus the Heikes votes let Dan S. Sullivan absorb RCV transfers, and the last-week spoiler/criminal-investigation stories blunt Peltola's polled edge.
AK.reasoning: Peltola won the top-four primary 49.5-41.4, leads most October polls by 1-5 (NYT/Siena +7, Fabrizio/Impact +5) and outraised Sullivan $36.9M to $14.1M. But the same-name candidate and Heikes bleed points and their transfers likely flow to Sullivan, while Oct. 28-30 spoiler revelations and investigations target her campaign, turning a polled edge into a coin flip she edges narrowly.

FL.key_factor: In a state Trump carried by 13, Moody's incumbent standing against a Jacksonville state legislator with a DSA label is nearly dispositive.
FL.reasoning: Moody leads every credible poll by 4-7 (NYT/Siena 50-44, UNF 49-45, Mason-Dixon 50-40), with debatable partisan-D outliers at 47. Nixon's socialist branding, the DSCC's other commitments, and a 1.5M registration edge favor R; Obama's late endorsement cannot move an R+13 special-electorate.意料之外 small chance a wave-plus-low-turnout special delivers Nixon很长 shot.

IA.key_factor: A rare open-seat race in R+13 with Turek's $24.3M-to-$14.1M money edge and a D-wave environment just outweighing Hinson's name recognition.
IA.reasoning: Polls zigzag: Marist (RV +7 Turek), Suffolk +4, YouGov +1 versus co/efficient +2 Hinson and NPA +3 Hinson. Averages give Turek +1 to +2 with the better trajectory and $21M spent. Iowa's R+13 baseline and 2014-style final-week R convergence are the main risks, but the trailing-position recuperation odds favor the D.

KS.key_factor: Hamilton has led or tied every credible October poll (WaPo/SSPG +9, CNN +4, Emerson +3-5, YouGov +3) while Marshall's 700-patient-lawsuit story and the Trump-rally slur dominate coverage.
KS.reasoning: Kansas's R+16 baseline has never elected a Democratic senator, and SLF redirected ~$30M here, showing GOP urgency. Hamilton is a first-time candidate at age 62 with 34.6% primary share, which caps his ceiling. But the cumulative vibe — consistent leads money rounds ($19.2M-to-$7.5M) and scandal-dominating coverage — outweigh the R floor.

ME.key_factor: Collins trails by 2-9 in every credible October poll (CNN +4 Jackson, Marist RV +9, UNH +4, NYT/Siena +3) with Trump's approval at 37-40% nationally.
ME.reasoning: The ProPublica pay-to-play story nationalized what was historically Collins's brand armor; Jackson's $26.9M matches her $25.2M. Collins survived 2020 with a massive final-week overperformance and has 30 years of cross-party appeal in a D+7 state that Trump lost three times; that resilience makes it close, but the wave-level national environment and story dominance point D.

MI.key_factor: In the most expensive Senate race in state history ($243M), El-Sayed consistently polls +4-8 (MSU/Verasight +6/+8, Marist +7 RV, Glengariff +6, CNN +3) with twice Rogers's fundraising.
MI.reasoning: El-Sayed's narrow 48.45% primary win over Haley Stevens was followed by her definitive endorsement and $53.8M raised versus Rogers's $23M. Rogers lost the 2024 race by 0.3 in a Trump +1.4 state; in a midterm with Trump at 36-38% approval the correlation breaks his way. R outside spending ($35M to $14.6M) narrows but closes a 5-point gap.

MN.key_factor: Flanagan leads every reliable poll by 3-14 (NYT/Siena 54-40, SurveyUSA +7, Mason-Dixon +4, GQR +8) after a 59% DFL primary and Obama's endorsement.
MN.reasoning: Trump carried Minnesota by just 1.4 in 2024, making this theoretically flippable, but in a midterm with the incumbent party underwater the celebrity broadcaster's R+credibility and Trump's Oct. 12 endorsement aren't closing a 7-9 point gap. Early vote volume and D-party unity lock in a hold.

NC.key_factor: Cooper leads by 7-14 in five straight credible polls with a $36M cash cushion ($9.1M on hand versus $902K) as SLF canceling ~$30M here signals national R retreat.
NC.reasoning: Cooper is a two-term governor with a 20-year NC favorability track record; Whatley is a first-time statewide contender even with RNC chair national-committee resources. The 2020 Cunningham polling overshoot (+5, lost by 1.8) and a Southern R base are the only serious warnings on an otherwise overwhelming D-flip reading.

NE.key_factor: With no Democrat on the ballot and Osborn mirroring his 2024 46.5%, the race is structural R+20 versus outside-money wave ($35.1M pro-Osborn versus $25.5M pro-R).
NE.reasoning: October polls split evenly (GBAO Osborn+1, YouGov Osborn+1, Impact Ricketts+2/+3, National Public Affairs Ricketts+3/+5, Echelon Ricketts+1). Osborn's $11M and occupational-labor identity give him a floor; Ricketts's incumbent apparatus and presidential-polling-skew guard the ceiling. Mike Marvin's departure endorsement funnels voters but his LMNOW line still picks up protest votes, fractionalizing Osborn's coalition.

NH.key_factor: Pappas holds +5-8 leads in every credible poll (YouGov +8, UNH +8, St. Anselm +7, CNN +6) with 4:1 cash ($23.7M vs $5.7M).
NH.reasoning: Sununu's family name and heavy R outside spending ($27.8M vs $23.8M) keep the margin under 5, and Trump narrowly lost New Hampshire in 2024 (D+2.8). Pappas's 65% primary, Shaheen's endorsement, and a retiring-incumbent normal-time baseline consolidate a sixish-point D lead that Sununu's visceral brand alone can't close.

OH.key_factor: Brown polls +3-7 in mid/late October (Suffolk +3, RedBox +3, Verasight +4, Beacon RV +7, YouGov +4) with $68.4M raised versus $19.9M.
OH.reasoning: Brown's brand power is such that 25% of likely voters already think he's the incumbent, and 71% support for a data-center pause attacks Husted's tax-break record directly. The 2024 presidential-year error (Brown led polls, lost by 3.6) and R outside spending ($9.3M vs $1.4M) keep this coin-flip-adjacent but on Brown's side.

SC.key_factor: An R+18 state defending its governor-appointed senator despite $1.9M versus $24.2M candidate spending, because structural partisanship explains even-money outcomes here.
SC.reasoning: Graham leads or ties most October surveys (ECU +4, Trafalgar +3, Rasmussen +4, NYT/Siena even) though partisan-D in-house polls put Andrews +1/+5. Andrews's runoff-nominee money advantage and outside D spending ($17.0M vs $12.7M) make this the closest SC Senate race in a generation, but a D+seventeen... no, a Republican +18 presidential baseline and appointee-of-Trump-and-Thune consolidation hold the seat.

TX.key_factor: Talarico leads by 2-6 in most credible polls (YouGov +6, NYT/Siena +6, Univision +5, Marist +4) with a $146M-to-$22.3M financial blowout against Paxton's R+13.7 base.
TX.reasoning: Paxton skipped debates, carries impeachment-era notoriety, and is facing record D turnout in a D-wave environment; registration-backlog coverage (~600K unprocessed applications) injects election-administration risk. Cor Strategies (R) flipped to Paxton+4 and red-state Senate polling has historically favored R by 2-4, so a structural-R floor keeps this razor-thin either way.

upset_watch.why: Sullivan trails by only 1-5 in polls, the RCV tabulation consolidates the Heikes and Sullivan Jr. ballots in his favor, and the closing-days spoiler-candidate and criminal-investigation stories against Peltola leave the incumbent a near-even chance despite watermark-level polling.
